$comment: 38 California city and county minimum wage ordinances -- more than the rest of the country combined. Two things make California local rates a distinctive trap: they adjust on TWO different cycles (January 1 and July 1), so any single annual refresh leaves half of them stale, and none of them permits a tip credit, because state law forbids it everywhere in California. Rates here are the ones IN EFFECT on this file's asOf date (2026-09-08), i.e. the July 1, 2026 figures for July-cycle cities and the January 1, 2026 figures for the rest. The 11 July-cycle jurisdictions (10 cities plus unincorporated LA County) also carry a historicalPredecessorOf variant with the July 2025-June 2026 figure that was in effect before this file's own headline number, so a checkDate earlier in 2026 resolves correctly too.

sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session for the July 2025 - June 2026 figures now carried as historicalPredecessorOf entries on each of the ten July-cycle cities: Alameda $17.46, Berkeley $19.18, Emeryville $19.90, Fremont $17.75, Los Angeles $17.87, Milpitas $18.20, Pasadena $18.04, San Francisco $19.18, Santa Monica $17.81, and Malibu's own one-year-suspended $17.27 (held two full years rather than one, per its city council's own suspension of its scheduled increase).

sources.title: Unincorporated Los Angeles County minimum wage, July 1, 2025 step ($17.81)
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session: the rate increased from $17.27 to $17.81 effective 2025-07-01, in effect through 2026-06-30, before the step to $18.47 this file's own headline figure carries.

knownGaps: Employer-size tiers are recorded only where a city publishes one (Hayward, Novato, Sonoma). Cities not carrying a tier apply one rate to all employers.

Several California cities ALSO run sector-specific minimum wages (hotel and airport workers in Los Angeles, hotel workers in Santa Monica, Long Beach, Glendale and West Hollywood). All five are now carried in sectoral/CA-sectoral-2026.json rather than here -- Glendale has no general local minimum wage ordinance of its own, only its hotel-worker one, which is why it has no entry in THIS file's own jurisdictions list.
A few of these ordinances exempt very small employers or government/nonprofit employers on their own terms; those coverage tests are not modelled per-city.
